title: The production VM
claim: Only NGINX answers web traffic from the internet. The dashboard, the API and the database listen on the VM's loopback address, and PM2 keeps the two apps running.

nodes.title: DNS
nodes.desc: 4 names, all pointing at the VM

nodes.title: NGINX
nodes.desc: HTTPS for all 4 names; port 80 only redirects

nodes.title: API
nodes.desc: the only app with the DB password

steps: A browser looks the name up in DNS, gets the VM's address and connects on port 443. All four names (`compostiq.win`, `www`, `dashboard`, `api`) point at this one VM, and one Let's Encrypt certificate covers them all.
NGINX chooses a site by the name that was asked for. `dashboard.compostiq.win` goes to the dashboard on `127.0.0.1:8050`.
The dashboard builds each page on the server and calls the API over loopback, never through NGINX. A signed-in user's browser never talks to the API itself.
Only the API has the database password. PostgreSQL listens on `127.0.0.1:5432`, and that port is never opened to the outside.

steps.text: `compostiq.win` is plain HTML. Its folder is mounted straight from the repo, so a `git pull` publishes a change with no restart. Its live figures ask `/api/public/*`, which NGINX passes to the API's `/public/*`.

Devices send readings to `api.compostiq.win`, and researchers' own scripts call `/research/*` there with a research key. Sign-in and pairing requests on this name are limited to 10 a minute per address before they reach the API; `/research/*` has no limit.

notes: PM2 runs the dashboard and the API from `deploy/pm2/ecosystem.config.js`. It restarts either app when it crashes or passes 500 MB, and starts both again after a reboot. NGINX and PostgreSQL are ordinary systemd services.
PM2 reads the one `.env` file and gives each app only the settings it needs, which is how the dashboard never sees `DATABASE_URL`.
SSH is not part of this picture: the repo holds no firewall settings, and a deploy is done by logging in to the VM.
